(a) Designation of Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering as the Official With Principal Responsibility for Development and Demonstration of Directed Energy Weapons.—Subsection (a)(1) of section 219 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2017 (Public Law 114–328; 10 U.S.C. 2431 note) is amended by striking “Not later” and all that follows through “Department of Defense” and inserting “The Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering shall serve”. 
    (b) Prototyping and Demonstration Program.—Such section is further amended by adding at the end the following new subsection:“(c) Prototyping and Demonstration Program.—“(1) Establishment.—The Secretary of Defense, acting through the Under Secretary, shall establish a program on the prototyping and demonstration of directed energy weapon systems to build and maintain the military superiority of the United States by—“(A) accelerating, when feasible, the fielding of directed energy weapon prototypes that would help counter technological advantages of potential adversaries of the United States; and“(B) supporting the military departments, the combatant commanders, and other relevant defense agencies and entities in developing prototypes and demonstrating operational utility of high energy lasers and high powered microwave weapon systems.“(2) Guidelines.—(A) Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2018, the Under Secretary shall issue guidelines for the operation of the program established under paragraph (1), including the following:“(i) Criteria required for an application for funding by a military department, defense agency or entity, or a combatant command.“(ii) The priorities, based on validated requirements or capability gaps, for fielding prototype directed energy weapon system technologies developed by research funding of the Department or industry.“(iii) Criteria for evaluation of an application for funding or changes to policies or acquisition and business practices by such a department, agency, or command for purposes of improving the effectiveness and efficiency of the program.“(B) Funding for a military department, defense agency, or combatant command under the program established under paragraph (1) may only be available for advanced technology development, prototyping, and demonstrations in which the Department of Defense maintains management of the technical baseline and a primary emphasis on technology transition and evaluating military utility to enhance the likelihood that the particular directed energy weapon system will meet the Department end user’s need.“(3) Applications for funding.—(A) Not less frequently than once each year, the Under Secretary shall solicit from the heads of the military departments, the defense agencies, and the combatant commands applications for funding under the program established under paragraph (1) to be used to enter into contracts, cooperative agreements, or other transaction agreements entered into pursuant to section 2371b of title 10, United States Code, with appropriate entities for the prototyping or commercialization of technologies.“(B) Nothing in this section shall be construed to require any official of the Department of Defense to provide funding under the program to any congressional earmark as defined pursuant to clause 9 of rule XXI of the Rules of the House of Representatives or any congressionally directed spending item as defined pursuant to paragraph 5 of rule XLIV of the Standing Rules of the Senate.“(4) Funding.—(A) Except as provided in subparagraph (B) and subject to the availability of appropriations for such purpose, of the funds authorized to be appropriated by the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2018 or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2018 for research, development, test, and evaluation, defense-wide, up to $100,000,000 may be available to the Under Secretary to allocate to the military departments, the defense agencies, and the combatant commands to carry out the program established under paragraph (1).“(B) Not more than half of the amounts made available under subparagraph (A) may be allocated as described in such paragraph until the Under Secretary—“(i) develops the strategic plan required by subsection (a)(2)(A); and“(ii) submits such strategic plan to the congressional defense committees.“(5) Under secretary defined.—In this subsection, the term ‘Under Secretary’ means the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering in the Under Secretary’s capacity as the official with principal responsibility for the development and demonstration of directed energy weapons pursuant to subsection (a)(1).”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that soliciting applications, issuing guidelines, and submitting a strategic plan to the congressional defense committees amount to consultation. Every actor involved is inside the federal government: the Under Secretary, military departments, defense agencies, combatant commands, and Congress. The guidelines govern an internal DoD funding program rather than a public rulemaking, and funding applications are not participation in any case. Industry is mentioned only as a source of technology or as a contract recipient, not as a party consulted on a federal decision.
fable.s: the Under Secretary shall solicit from the heads of the military departments, the defense agencies, and the combatant commands applications for funding under the program

qwen_block.w: The section describes an internal Department of Defense process where the Under Secretary solicits funding applications from other federal officials (heads of military departments, defense agencies, and combatant commands). The definition explicitly excludes applications for grants or benefits and excludes coordination between federal agencies or officials. There is no requirement for consultation with non-federal entities, public comment, or advisory boards with outside members.
qwen_block.s: Not less frequently than once each year, the Under Secretary shall solicit from the heads of the military departments, the defense agencies, and the combatant commands applications for funding under the program established under paragraph (1)
qwen_block.b:
1.  **Think briefly**: The section describes the establishment of a "Prototyping and Demonstration Program" within the Department of Defense. It details the roles of the Secretary of Defense and the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering. It mentions that the Under Secretary will solicit applications for funding from "heads of the military departments, the defense agencies, and the combatant commands." It also mentions that the program supports these entities and that funding may be used for contracts with "appropriate entities" (which could include industry). However, the core decision-making process described is internal to the federal government: the Under Secretary (a federal official) solicits applications from other federal officials (heads of military departments, etc.) and allocates funds among them. The definition states that "consultation or coordination BETWEEN federal agencies or federal officials... is not participation." The "appropriate entities" mentioned for contracts are likely industry partners, but the text describes the *solicitation of applications* from federal heads, not a consultation with outside parties before a decision. The application process itself is explicitly excluded ("It does not include applications for benefits or grants"). There is no mention of public comment periods, advisory boards with non-federal members, or consultation with states/tribes/public before the federal decision. The interaction is purely intra-governmental (DoD components). Therefore, the label is "No".

opus.w: The only parties involved are the Under Secretary, military departments, defense agencies, combatant commands and the congressional defense committees, all inside the federal government. The guidelines are internal program rules, not regulations or a public comment process. Funding applications and reports to Congress are listed exclusions, so the procedural wording does not make this participation by outside parties.
opus.s: the Under Secretary shall solicit from the heads of the military departments, the defense agencies, and the combatant commands applications for funding under the program established under paragraph (1)

Label: **No**. Every actor in this section is inside the federal government.

1. **The tempting reading:** Three things look procedural. The Under Secretary must issue guidelines, which could look like rulemaking. He must collect funding applications every year. And a strategic plan goes to the congressional defense committees. None of these brings in anyone outside the federal government. The guidelines are internal operating rules for a Defense Department program, not regulations. They govern applications from the military departments, defense agencies and combatant commands, all of which are federal. Applying for funding is excluded by the definition anyway. Sending the plan to Congress is a report that stays inside the government. The contracts with "appropriate entities" are how money gets spent, not a way for outsiders to help make the decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section describes a process where the Under Secretary of Defense solicits funding applications from heads of military departments, defense agencies, and combatant commands. All these entities are part of the federal government (Department of Defense). The definition explicitly states that consultation or coordination between federal agencies or officials is not participation. There is no requirement to consult with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_chat.s: (3) Applications for funding.—(A) Not less frequently than once each year, the Under Secretary shall solicit from the heads of the military departments, the defense agencies, and the combatant commands applications for funding under the program established under paragraph (1)
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the solicitation of applications from military departments and combatant commands constitutes participation because it involves input from various entities before funding decisions are made. However, military departments, defense agencies, and combatant commands are all components of the federal government (specifically the Department of Defense). Therefore, this is intra-governmental coordination, not participation by outside parties.
